# nish/net/quic-datagram

a fixed ring of QUIC DATAGRAM payloads (RFC 9221), one each way per connection: what the application queued to send, waiting for room in a packet and in the congestion window, and what the peer sent, waiting for the application to read it. Sans-IO, like the rest of `nish/net`; `nish/net/quic`'s `QuicConnection` owns both rings and the application reaches them through its `sendDatagram` and `readDatagram`.

```ts
import {
  QuicDatagramQueue,
} from "nish/net/quic-datagram";
```

A ring of `entries` datagram payloads of at most `entrySize` bytes each, oldest first.

<scalar-detail title="Fixed">

A ring is `entries` payloads of at most `entrySize` bytes,
allocated once; a payload is copied in and out, and nothing allocates
after the ring is made. A datagram is unreliable by definition (RFC 9221
§5), so a full ring refuses the next rather than growing, and what the
peer sends past a full receive ring, or past `entrySize`, is dropped and
counted in `dropped`.

</scalar-detail>

Written from RFC 9221, in this module's own structure; nothing here is
ported from another implementation. Private names carry the
`quicDatagram` prefix (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

## QuicDatagramQueue

A ring of `entries` datagram payloads of at most `entrySize` bytes each, oldest first.

```ts
class QuicDatagramQueue
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicDatagramQueue( entries: i32, entrySize: i32, )` |  |
| `count: i32` |  |
| `data: u8[]` | Entry `k`'s bytes are `data[k * entrySize ..]`, `lengths[k]` of them. |
| `dropped: i32` | Datagrams refused for want of room or for their size, which the peer's side counts as dropped. |
| `entrySize: i32` |  |
| `head: i32` |  |
| `lengths: i32[]` |  |
| `capacity(): i32` | How many datagrams the ring holds at most. |
| `drop(): void` | Forgets the oldest datagram. |
| `peekLength(): i32` | The oldest datagram's length, or -1 when the ring is empty. |
| `pop(buf: u8[], at: i32, cap: i32): i32` | Copies the oldest datagram into `buf` at `at` and forgets it. Answers its length, -1 when the ring is empty, or -2, keeping it, when it does not fit in `cap` bytes from `at` inside `buf`. |
| `push(buf: u8[], from: i32, length: i32): boolean` | Copies `buf[from .. from + length)` in as the newest datagram. Answers whether it could: not when the ring is full, nor for a payload past `entrySize` or a window outside `buf`, each of which counts in `dropped`. |
| `putFrame(buf: u8[], at: i32, end: i32): i32` | Writes the oldest datagram as a DATAGRAM frame into `buf[at .. end)` and forgets it. Answers the offset past the frame, or `at` when the ring is empty or the frame does not fit, keeping it for the next packet. |
| `reset(): void` | Empties the ring, for a connection slot reused for another peer. |
